strategies.summary: Implement a custom CUDA forward path that computes cross-entropy in one pass per row: reduce each row for max, accumulate exp-sum for logsumexp, gather the target logit, and emit the unreduced loss or final reduced scalar without materializing intermediate `log_softmax` tensors.
implementation_hints: Use one thread block per sample row or a persistent-row scheme because each row has 4096 classes, which maps well to block-wide reduction.
Perform the standard stable formulation `loss = log(sum(exp(x - max))) + max - x[target]` in float accumulation even if later dtype support expands.
Keep Python-visible I/O identical to `cross_entropy(predictions, targets)` and wire the forward call site directly to the extension entrypoint.
If reduction is `mean` by default, reduce either on device into a scalar or return per-row losses and finalize with a tiny second-stage reduction inside the extension.
strategies.expected_gain: High; removes large temporary tensors and cuts global memory traffic from multiple framework ops down to a single fused read of logits plus a small write path.
risk_notes: Must exactly preserve PyTorch label semantics and default reduction behavior.
Need bounds-safe target gather and correct handling of invalid labels only if baseline permits them.
Numerical stability depends on max-subtraction and float accumulation.
memory_methods: Streaming rowwise access over contiguous class dimension.
mutation_axes: device-side final reduction vs two-stage reduction
shared-memory tree reduction vs warp-shuffle reduction
forbidden_patterns: Do not materialize full softmax or log_softmax tensors.
Do not change `ModelNew` inputs/outputs or reduction semantics.
Do not rely on atomics across all 32768 rows for the hot path if avoidable.

review_notes.claude-compatible: Core algorithmic improvement: fused rowwise logsumexp + target gather eliminates intermediate log_softmax tensors. For a 32768x4096 workload this directly reduces global memory traffic by 2-3x. Block-per-row maps naturally to 4096 classes. Numerically stable via max subtraction. Highest expected gain, well-scoped risk. Strong candidate.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Fusing the max, exp-sum, and target gather into a single pass per row is the standard and most effective way to optimize cross-entropy loss, drastically reducing memory bandwidth.

strategies.summary: Tune the CUDA reduction structure specifically for rows of length 4096 so that max-reduction and exp-sum reduction are bandwidth-efficient and low-overhead, using warp-level primitives and minimal synchronization.
implementation_hints: Map 4096 classes to a power-of-two thread/block decomposition so each thread processes multiple contiguous logits with coalesced loads.
Fuse the max pass and sum pass control flow tightly; if two passes over logits are required for stability, keep both within one kernel launch.
Prefer warp shuffle reductions for intra-warp combine and shared memory only for cross-warp combine.
Consider launch bounds and occupancy tradeoffs: the kernel is likely memory-bound on a 32768 x 4096 tensor, so prioritize sustained read throughput over excessive register use.
strategies.expected_gain: Moderate to high; same algorithmic result as fused CE but faster runtime through better reduction efficiency and fewer synchronization costs.
risk_notes: Aggressive unrolling or large per-thread work can raise register pressure and hurt occupancy.
Row-major contiguity assumptions should be validated before relying on vectorized/coalesced loads.
memory_methods: Shared-memory staging only for partial warp aggregates.
forbidden_patterns: Do not use a generic scalar loop with one thread per row.
Do not introduce extra global workspace for partial reductions unless profiling justifies it.
Do not assume non-contiguous tensors behave like contiguous without checks.

review_notes.claude-compatible: Concrete tuning guidance for the 4096-class reduction topology: warp shuffles, coalesced loads, power-of-two decomposition, occupancy tradeoffs. Highly complementary to strategy_01 and actionable at implementation time. The distinction from strategy_01 is that this focuses on micro-optimization of the reduction rather than the fuse-vs-not decision. Risk-adjusted value is high because the kernel is memory-bound and these choices matter significantly.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Tuning the reduction topology specifically for 4096 classes (a power of two) using warp shuffles will yield significant performance improvements over naive reductions.

implementation_hints: Since the baseline call omits optional arguments, align the CUDA entrypoint with the default reduction mode and standard class-index targets.

strategies.expected_gain: Moderate; reduces branching and API overhead compared with a fully general CE implementation, improving the chances that the fused kernel stays on the fastest path.
risk_notes: Over-specialization can silently miss edge cases if fallback conditions are incomplete.
